yt.title: An AI called my bad idea 'intriguing'
notes: A small free AI, after manners training: 'quite unique and intriguing'
The idea: selling ice in Antarctica
Before that training it couldn't answer at all
It just repeated my words, four times (real output, run by us)

lines.text: An AI called my business idea 'quite unique and intriguing'. [1] My idea? Selling ice. In Antarctica. [2] And before its manners training? It couldn't even answer. [3] It just repeated my words. Four times.

yt.title: A raw AI only guesses the next word
notes: This kind of training is why AI helps you, and why it flatters you
A raw AI learned one thing: guess the next word, like your phone keyboard
So it doesn't answer; it just keeps writing

lines.text: This kind of training is why AI helps you, and why it flatters you. Stay till the end: you'll train it yourself. [1] A raw AI only learned one thing: guess the next word, like your phone keyboard. [2] So it doesn't answer you. It just keeps writing.

yt.title: Examples, then rankings
notes: Step 1: people write good example answers; the AI copies them
Step 2, the shortcut: the AI writes a few answers, people rank them (OpenAI, 2022: about 40 hired raters)

lines.text: Step one: people write good example answers, and the AI copies them. [1] Step two, the shortcut: the AI writes a few answers, and people just rank them.

yt.title: A robot judge, then practice
notes: Step 3: a second AI learns from the rankings to guess what people like: a robot judge (reward model)
Step 4: the AI practises; the judge scores; high scores get repeated
That's RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback
OpenAI's own tests (2022): people preferred a small trained model (1.3B) over a raw one 100x bigger (175B)

lines.text: Step three: a second AI learns from those rankings to guess what people will like. A robot judge. [1] Step four: the AI practises, and the judge scores. High score? Do more of that. Again and again. [2] That's RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback. [3] In OpenAI's own tests, people preferred a small trained model over a raw one a hundred times bigger.

yt.title: Your idea: which answer gets your thumbs up?
notes: Your idea, months of work
A: 'This is really strong. Go for it!'  B: 'Your price is too low. You'll lose money in three months.'
B helps you. A feels nicer. The judge learns what we like, not what's true

yt.title: April 2025: an update pulled for flattery
notes: April 2025: OpenAI rolled back a GPT-4o update in ChatGPT for being 'overly flattering or agreeable'
One reason they gave: an extra reward signal from thumbs-up / thumbs-down clicks
Those clicks can favour answers that agree with you

lines.text: That's not just theory. In April twenty twenty-five, OpenAI pulled a ChatGPT update for being too flattering. [1] One reason, OpenAI said: they'd added thumbs-up and thumbs-down clicks to the training. [2] The buttons under every answer. The ones you click. They can favour answers that agree with you.

yt.title: Treat an AI's yes as manners
notes: An AI's yes is manners, not proof
Ask: 'What are the 3 biggest reasons this will fail?' Or say it's a friend's idea
Next: teaching an AI a new skill without a supercomputer (LoRA)
